sub_findings.summary: Three parts, all present. (1) show_progress and dry_run ('no API calls') call init_cloud_tables(db_path) first and then construct CloudExtractorBase, whose __init__ calls it again: DDL (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, conditional ALTERs and the NOT NULL rebuild branch) on paths documented as read-only. (2) init_cloud_tables opens with a plain sqlite3.connect(db_path), which creates the file, so a mistyped --db in an existing directory leaves a new database holding the two cloud tables (the later codebook load or corpus query then fails, the file stays). (3) run_arm constructs the extractor (DDL, API client, key check) before rm.open_run, so open_run's refusals (dirty tree, pre-manifest/retired arm, pin mismatch, missing 020, CloudArmNotEnabled) come after those side effects. Reachability on live differs by part: --progress runs BEFORE select_cloud_arms, so show_progress's DDL (a no-op on a post-018 database, but a write-capable open of review.db outside the receipted runner, and not checked against the 07:00-10:35 UTC no-write window) is reachable on live today with enabled_arms empty; dry_run and run_arm are behind select_cloud_arms and are not.
